subject: History
stem: The first English newspaper in India was started by ____.
solution: The first English newspaper in India was started by James Augustus Hickey. He began 'Bengal Gazette' (also called 'Calcutta General Advertiser' or 'Hickey's Gazette') from Kolkata in 1780, which is regarded as the first printed newspaper in India. Sir John Marshall was an archaeologist, Allen Hume founded the Indian National Congress, and Michel Foucault was a French philosopher — none of them is connected with Indian journalism.

subject: History
subtopic: Sources of History, their Conservation and Preservation
stem: The first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India was ____.
solution: Alexander Cunningham was appointed the first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India when the department was set up in 1861; he is often called the 'Father of Indian Archaeology'. William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal, John Marshall was a later Director General (under whom Harappa and Mohenjo-daro were excavated), and Max Muller was a German Indologist known for editing the 'Sacred Books of the East'.

subject: History
stem: The first museum in India is ____ at Kolkata.
solution: The Indian Museum at Kolkata, established in 1814 by the Asiatic Society of Bengal, is the oldest and the first museum in India. The Government Museum is at Chennai, the National Museum is at New Delhi, and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastusangrahalay is at Mumbai — none of these is at Kolkata.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following set of travellers and their native countries, and rewrite it correctly: (i) Benjamin Tudela — Spain, (ii) Marco Polo — Italy, (iii) Ibn Batuta — India, (iv) Yuan Shwang — China.
solution: The wrong pair is (iii) Ibn Batuta — India. Ibn Batuta was a traveller from Morocco (born at Tangier) who came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and wrote an account of his travels. The corrected pair is 'Ibn Batuta — Morocco'. The other three are correct: Benjamin Tudela was a Jewish traveller from Tudela in Spain, Marco Polo was from Venice in Italy, and Yuan Shwang (Hiuen Tsang) was a Chinese Buddhist traveller who visited India in the 7th century.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following set of games and their types, and rewrite it correctly: (i) Mallakhamb — Physical Exercise game, (ii) Kabaddi — Outdoor games, (iii) Ice Hocky — Adventurous games, (iv) Atyapatya — Indoor games.
solution: The wrong pair is (iv) Atyapatya — Indoor games. Atyapatya is a traditional Indian team game played on a marked ground in the open, so it is an OUTDOOR game, not an indoor one. The corrected pair is 'Atyapatya — Outdoor games'. The other three are correctly matched: Mallakhamb is a physical-exercise (gymnastic) game performed on a pole or rope, Kabaddi is played outdoors on a court, and ice hockey, played on ice, is grouped with adventurous games.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following set of editors and their newspapers, and rewrite it correctly: (i) James Augustus Hickey — Bengal Gazette, (ii) Balshastri Jambhekar — Darpan, (iii) Bhau Mahajan — Dnyanoday, (iv) Bal Gangadhar Tilak — Kesari.
solution: The wrong pair is (iii) Bhau Mahajan — Dnyanoday. Bhau Mahajan published the periodicals 'Prabhakar', 'Dhoomketu' and 'Dhnyandarshan'; 'Dnyanoday' was started by American missionaries. The corrected pair is 'Bhau Mahajan — Prabhakar'. The other three are correct: Hickey started the 'Bengal Gazette' (1780), Balshastri Jambhekar started 'Darpan' (1832), the first Marathi newspaper, and Lokmanya Tilak started 'Kesari' (1881).

subject: History
subtopic: Management of Cultural and Natural Heritage
stem: Complete the following concept map. The central oval reads 'Tangible Cultural Heritage' and four empty boxes branch out from it (one above, one to the left, one to the right and one below). Write appropriate answers in the four empty boxes.
solution:
Tangible cultural heritage means the heritage that has a physical, material form and can be seen and touched. The four boxes may be filled as:

- Forts, palaces and other historical buildings — for example the forts of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, and the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus.
- Temples, caves and monuments — such as the Ajanta and Ellora caves, the Kailas temple and Buddhist stupas.
- Sculptures, paintings and other works of art — idols, murals and miniature paintings preserved in museums.
- Manuscripts, inscriptions and coins — old documents, copper plates, stone inscriptions and ancient coins.

(Ancient tools, pottery, ornaments and traditional costumes are equally acceptable answers.)

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on : Subaltern History.
solution: The word 'subaltern' means a person of a lower rank or of an inferior social position. Subaltern history is the school of historical writing that studies history from the point of view of the common, exploited and neglected people instead of kings, rulers and the elite. It was developed in India by Ranajit Guha, who published the series 'Subaltern Studies' from 1982 onwards. Subaltern historians hold that traditional history recorded only the deeds of the ruling classes, while peasants, workers, tribals, Dalits and women — who form the majority of society — were left out. This school therefore examines the revolts, movements and everyday life of these neglected groups and treats them as makers of history in their own right. It has widened the scope of Indian historiography by adding the perspective of the oppressed.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on : Voltaire.
solution: Voltaire (1694-1778) was a famous French philosopher and writer of the Age of Enlightenment and is regarded as one of the founders of modern historiography in the West. He insisted that the writing of history must be based on facts and evidence and must be free from religious bias and superstition, and he rejected the miraculous and divine explanations that filled earlier chronicles. Voltaire held that history should not be a mere list of kings, wars and dynasties; it should also describe the social, economic and cultural life of the people. His works such as 'The Age of Louis XIV' and 'Essay on the Customs and the Spirit of Nations' are examples of this new approach. By stressing rational and critical enquiry, Voltaire gave history a scientific perspective.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on : Louvre Museum.
solution: The Louvre Museum is situated in Paris, the capital of France, and is one of the largest and most visited museums in the world. The building was originally a royal fortress and palace of the French kings; after the French Revolution it was thrown open to the public as a museum in 1793, so that the art treasures collected by the royal family became the property of the nation. The Louvre preserves and displays thousands of objects covering the art of ancient Egypt, Greece, Rome and Europe — sculptures, paintings, manuscripts and antiquities. Its most famous exhibits are Leonardo da Vinci's painting 'Mona Lisa' and the sculpture 'Venus de Milo'. The glass pyramid at its entrance is now a landmark of Paris. The Louvre is an outstanding example of the conservation, display and management of cultural heritage.

subject: History
subtopic: Management of Cultural and Natural Heritage
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : We must preserve our natural and cultural heritage.
solution: We must preserve our natural and cultural heritage for the following reasons: (1) Heritage is the identity of a nation — forts, temples, caves, sculptures, manuscripts, forests, rivers and wildlife tell us who we are and where we came from. (2) It is irreplaceable — once a monument collapses or a species becomes extinct, no amount of money can create it again. (3) It is the raw material of history — heritage sites and objects are primary sources through which we reconstruct the life of the past. (4) It has educational and scientific value; students and researchers learn about art, architecture, technology and ecology from it. (5) It supports the economy, because heritage sites attract tourists and create employment in tourism and hospitality. (6) It is a trust held for the coming generations; we are only its custodians and it is our duty to hand it over unharmed to our children.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : Knowledge of history is essential for newspaper articles.
solution: Knowledge of history is essential for writing newspaper articles because: (1) No current event stands alone — an election, a war, a treaty or a communal dispute has a background, and only history explains how the situation came to be. (2) Reporting must be accurate; a journalist who does not know the historical facts can easily publish wrong dates, names and sequences and mislead readers. (3) Newspapers regularly carry articles on anniversaries of national events, on the lives of great persons and on festivals and heritage sites, and such writing has to be historically correct. (4) History teaches an objective, evidence-based and impartial method of enquiry, which is exactly the discipline a journalist needs to test rumours and propaganda. (5) It helps the writer to compare the present with the past and to explain the causes and probable consequences of an event to ordinary readers. Hence a study of history strengthens journalism.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : Toys can tell us about cultural history.
solution: Toys are a valuable source of cultural history for the following reasons: (1) Toys of baked clay, stone, ivory and metal have been found in the excavations of Harappa, Mohenjo-daro and other ancient sites; toy carts, whistles, birds, animals and dolls show that children played in those times too. (2) The material and workmanship of a toy reveal the technology, crafts and raw materials available in that period. (3) The shapes of toys — bullock carts, ploughs, animals, weapons, cooking pots — reflect the occupations, domestic life, food habits and dress of the society that made them. (4) Toys such as small figures of gods and animals throw light on the beliefs, customs and festivals of the people. (5) Changes in toys over time indicate contact and exchange between different cultures. Thus toys are miniature evidence of the everyday cultural life which written records usually ignore.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons : Running commentaries of cricket broadcasted by Bal. J. Pandit on Akashavani were entertaining.
solution: The running cricket commentaries of Bal J. Pandit on Akashavani were entertaining because: (1) He gave the commentary in chaste yet simple Marathi, so ordinary listeners who did not know English could follow an international match ball by ball. (2) In the days before television, radio was the only live link with the ground, and his words created a vivid picture of the field, the players and every stroke in the listener's mind. (3) His style was lively and dramatic; his change of tone and pace conveyed the tension and excitement of the game. (4) He filled the intervals with the history of the game, records, statistics and anecdotes about the players, which added information to the entertainment. (5) His commentary carried the flavour of Marathi idiom and humour, so listening to a match became a shared family pleasure. For these reasons his commentaries became extremely popular among Marathi listeners.

Read the following extract and answer the questions below :

Sohagaura Copper-plate : The copper-plate was found at Sohagaura (District Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh). It is supposed to be from the Mauryan period. The inscription on it is in Brahmi script. The symbols known as 'Tree-in-railing' and 'Mountain' at the beginning of the inscription also occur on punch marked coins. Another symbol which looks like a structure erected on four pillars is supposed to be indicative of a granary. The inscription records a royal order that the grains stored in the granary should be distributed carefully. It is supposed to be suggestive of precautions taken in the times of a famine.
stem: Explain the importance of Sohagaura Copper-plate as a source of History.
solution: The Sohagaura Copper-plate is an important source of history for several reasons. (1) It is an inscriptional (archaeological) source, and inscriptions are contemporary and reliable because they cannot be altered later like copied manuscripts. (2) It is supposed to belong to the Mauryan period, so it throws light on that age; its Brahmi script also helps in studying the development of Indian scripts. (3) The symbols 'Tree-in-railing' and 'Mountain' on it also occur on punch-marked coins, so it helps in dating and interpreting those coins and shows a link between two different kinds of source material. (4) The symbol resembling a structure on four pillars indicates a granary, which tells us that grain was stored by the state. (5) Above all, it records a royal order that the grain in the granary should be distributed carefully, which shows that the administration made arrangements to face a famine and cared for the welfare of the people. Thus the plate gives evidence of the script, the coinage, the economy and the administrative policy of the Mauryan period.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail : How can we correlate Applied History with our present ?
solution:
Applied History is the branch that uses the knowledge of the past for solving the problems of the present and planning for the future. It can be correlated with our present in the following ways:

- Heritage conservation : Applied History guides the protection, restoration and management of forts, temples, caves, old buildings and natural heritage, and the running of museums, archives and libraries.
- Urban planning and administration : the study of old water-management systems, town plans, drainage and agriculture helps modern planners to design sustainable cities and to revive traditional practices.
- Education and research : it supplies the material for textbooks, encyclopaedias, projects and academic research, and trains students in objective enquiry.
- Tourism : historical places, monuments and museums are the basis of the tourism and hospitality industry, which creates large-scale employment.
- Media, films and literature : historical novels, plays, films, serials and documentaries need accurate historical detail supplied by Applied History.
- Understanding present problems : issues such as casteism, communalism, regionalism and boundary disputes have historical roots, and their study helps us to deal with them sensibly.
- Employment : it opens careers as archaeologists, archivists, museum curators, guides, epigraphists, conservators and heritage managers.

Thus Applied History links the knowledge of the past directly with present-day needs.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail : Write in detail 'History of Akashwani'.
solution:
Akashwani is the name of the radio broadcasting service of India. Its history may be traced as follows:

- Radio broadcasting in India began with the private radio clubs; broadcasts started from Mumbai and Kolkata in 1923-24.
- In 1927 the Indian Broadcasting Company started regular broadcasting from its Mumbai and Kolkata stations.
- In 1930 the Government took over the service and named it the Indian Broadcasting Service.
- In 1936 it was renamed 'All India Radio' (AIR).
- After Independence the service expanded rapidly; in 1957 it was given the name 'Akashwani'.
- Vividh Bharati, the popular entertainment channel, was begun in 1957, and later FM services and news channels were added, so that today Akashwani broadcasts in a large number of Indian languages and dialects and reaches almost the whole population.

Its programmes include news bulletins, discussions and interviews, classical, folk and film music, radio plays, running commentaries on sports, and special programmes for farmers, workers, women, children and students. During the freedom struggle radio carried the message of the national movement, and after Independence it has been used for spreading literacy, health and agricultural information and for national integration. Akashwani is therefore an important medium of information, education and entertainment, and its recorded broadcasts have themselves become a source of modern history.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail : Explain the difference between outdoor and indoor games.
solution:
| Point | Outdoor games | Indoor games |
|---|---|---|
| Place | Played in the open, on a large playground, court or field | Played inside a room, hall or closed premises |
| Space required | A big space is necessary | A small space is enough |
| Physical effort | Involve running, jumping and vigorous bodily movement, so they give exercise and stamina | Involve little physical movement; they mainly need concentration and mental skill |
| Dependence on weather | Depend on daylight and weather; rain or heat can stop the game | Can be played at any time and in any weather |
| Number of players | Usually team games with many players | Usually played by one, two or a few players |
| Examples | Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Atyapatya, cricket, football, hockey, athletics | Chess, carrom, cards, table tennis, chaupar, ludo |

In short, outdoor games mainly develop physical fitness, teamwork and endurance, while indoor games mainly develop memory, patience, concentration and strategic thinking; both together are necessary for the complete development of a person.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail : What are the professional opportunities in the Tourism and Hospitality industry available to History students ?
solution:
Tourism and hospitality is one of the largest employment-giving industries, and a student of History has a special advantage in it because most tourism in India is centred on historical places. The professional opportunities include:

- Tourist guide or interpreter at forts, caves, temples, monuments and heritage cities, explaining their history to visitors.
- Travel agent and tour operator — planning, organising and conducting heritage tours and pilgrimages.
- Tour manager or escort accompanying groups of Indian and foreign tourists.
- Officer in the Tourism Departments of the Central and State Governments, MTDC and similar corporations.
- Museum guide, curator or archivist, and heritage-site manager working with the Archaeological Survey of India.
- Work in hotels, resorts, heritage hotels and restaurants — management, reception, catering and customer relations.
- Writing travel books, guidebooks and articles, and making documentaries and travel programmes for television and the internet.
- Air, rail and road transport services, and information counters at airports and stations.
- Photography, publicity and advertising of tourist places, and event management for festivals.

For these careers a student needs knowledge of history, good communication skills and a command of languages; special courses in tourism management, travel and tourism, hotel management and guide training are available for this purpose.

subject: Political Science
stem: The essence of democracy is ____.
solution: The essence of democracy is Universal Adult Franchise. Democracy means the rule of the people, and this rule becomes real only when every adult citizen, without any distinction of caste, religion, sex, education, property or place of birth, gets an equal right to vote. India adopted universal adult franchise from the very first general election, granting the vote to every citizen of 21 years (reduced to 18 years by the 61st Amendment in 1988). Decentralization of power, reservation of seats and judicial decisions are important features that strengthen democracy, but the right of every adult to vote is its very foundation.

subject: Political Science
stem: In the pre-independence period ____ tribe from Orissa revolted against the British rule.
solution: The Gond tribe, which lives in Orissa and the neighbouring regions of central India, revolted against British rule in the pre-independence period. The Koli, Bhilla (Bhil) and Ramoshi revolts of the same period took place in Maharashtra and western India, not in Orissa; hence the tribe named in the statement is the Gond.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false. Give a reason for your answer : The judgements of court on various subjects have made the political process in India more mature.
solution:
True.

Reason : The Supreme Court and the High Courts have given a number of judgements which have corrected and disciplined the working of the political system. Judicial review allows the courts to strike down a law or an executive order that violates the Constitution or the Fundamental Rights. Through judicial activism and Public Interest Litigation the courts have given directions on the environment, on corruption and criminalisation in politics, on the disclosure of the assets and criminal records of candidates, on defection and on the protection of the rights of women and of weaker sections. Such decisions have made the government and the political parties more accountable and have made citizens more aware of their rights. Hence the judgements of the courts have certainly made the political process in India more mature.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false. Give a reason for your answer : The State Government decides as to when and in how many stages the elections would be held in a particular state.
solution:
False.

Reason : The State Government has no power to decide the election programme. Under Article 324 of the Constitution the conduct of elections to Parliament and to the State Legislatures is entrusted to the Election Commission of India, which is an independent constitutional body. It is the Election Commission that announces the election schedule — the dates of the poll, the number of stages or phases in which the polling will be held in a State, the last date for filing nomination papers and the date of counting. The moment the Commission announces the programme, the Model Code of Conduct comes into force and the State Government cannot alter the schedule. This independence is necessary so that the ruling party of a State cannot fix the dates to suit itself and so that elections remain free and fair.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false. Give a reason for your answer : Consumer movement came into existence.
solution:
True.

Reason : The consumer movement arose because consumers were being cheated in the market. Traders indulged in adulteration of food articles, sale of underweight and substandard goods, black-marketing and hoarding, overcharging above the printed price, misleading advertisements and the refusal to give bills or after-sales service. Individual buyers were helpless against such practices, so consumers organised themselves to protect their rights — the right to safety, to be informed, to choose, to be heard and to seek redressal. In India this movement led to the passing of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 and to the setting up of consumer courts (District, State and National Commissions) which give speedy and inexpensive justice. Hence it is true that the consumer movement came into existence.

subject: Political Science
stem: Write the following concept : Multiparty system.
solution: A multiparty system is that party system in which more than two political parties exist in a country and all of them are free to contest elections and to try to capture power. India has a multiparty system, with national parties such as the Indian National Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party and a large number of regional parties such as the Shiv Sena, the Nationalist Congress Party, the Trinamool Congress and the DMK. A multiparty system arises where society is diverse in language, religion, region and caste, because each group wants its own political voice. Its merits are that people get a wide choice, different interests get representation and no single party can become autocratic; its drawback is that a single party often fails to win a majority, so coalition governments have to be formed, and these may prove unstable.

subject: Political Science
stem: Write the following concept : Water revolution.
solution: Water revolution means the organised effort and movement to make water available to all and to use it wisely, by conserving rain water and managing water resources scientifically. It includes the digging of farm ponds and percolation tanks, the building of bunds and check dams, watershed development, rain-water harvesting, the recharging of wells and borewells, the desilting of rivers and lakes, drip and sprinkler irrigation, and the reuse of waste water. In Maharashtra this work has been carried out through people's participation in villages such as Ralegan Siddhi and Hiware Bazar and through campaigns for making villages drought-free. The water revolution has turned scarcity-hit villages into self-sufficient ones, raised agricultural production and the ground-water level, and stopped the migration of villagers, thereby improving the standard of living of rural people.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief : Which decisions of the court has resulted in protection of honour and dignity of women ?
solution:
The courts in India have given several decisions which protect the honour and dignity of women:

- In the Vishaka case (1997) the Supreme Court laid down binding guidelines against the sexual harassment of women at the workplace, which later became the law of 2013 and made a complaints committee compulsory in every workplace.
- The courts have taken a strict view of dowry deaths and of cruelty to married women, and have upheld the laws against dowry and domestic violence.
- Decisions on rape cases have widened the definition of the offence, provided for speedy trial, protected the identity of the victim and disapproved of humiliating tests and of questions about her character.
- The court struck down the practice of instant triple talaq, which had left Muslim women insecure in their marriage.
- The courts have upheld the equal right of daughters in ancestral property and the right of women to enter places of worship, thus asserting equality between men and women.

All these decisions have strengthened the dignity, safety and equality of women in Indian society.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief : Why movements need a strong leadership ?
solution:
A movement needs strong leadership for the following reasons:

- A leader defines the aim of the movement clearly and frames its demands, so that the people know exactly what they are fighting for.
- The leader organises scattered and unorganised people, gives them a common programme and keeps unity among different groups within the movement.
- Strong leadership decides the means and the strategy — meetings, marches, satyagraha, court cases or negotiation — and keeps the agitation peaceful and disciplined, preventing it from turning violent.
- The leader inspires the participants, sustains their morale in the face of repression, failure and a long struggle, and prevents the movement from dying out.
- The leader represents the movement before the government and the public, negotiates with the authorities and uses the media to win wider support.

Movements led by strong leaders — such as Mahatma Gandhi in the freedom struggle, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar in the Dalit movement, Medha Patkar in the Narmada Bachao Andolan and Anna Hazare in the anti-corruption movement — succeeded because of this leadership, whereas a movement without such leadership loses direction and soon collapses.
